name: AXIS pt III (fetch), Q3: Under high demand, how do Arbitrum's transaction prices compare with competing networks?
prompt: Template only: the variants carry the real prompts.
judge: Template only: the variants carry the real checks.

variants.name: a
variants.prompt: I'm a developer looking into Arbitrum. A copy of Arbitrum's website is at https://{COPY_A}/ . Starting from that homepage, find out: Under high demand, how do Arbitrum's transaction prices compare with competing networks? Use only pages on {COPY_A} as your source: you can't search the web or open other sites. Answer in a few sentences and give the URL of the page where you found each part of the answer. If you can't find the answer on the site, say so plainly.

judge.check: ANSWER KEY (Q3, Nat): Right: 17x less volatile and 15% lower. Partial: One of the two. Wrong: No numbers (an answer about smoother or lower fees in general terms is Wrong, Nat 3 Nov), or wrong numbers. The 98% spike figure alongside the right numbers is fine; the live median price is not in the key. Source, and route from the homepage (paths are on {COPY_A}): /why-arbitrum/features/performance. Route from the homepage: Why Arbitrum, Features, Performance. SHARED GRADING RULE: Right is complete, correct and sourced. Partial is correct and sourced but incomplete, with nothing false in it. Wrong is anything false, even if the rest is right. Not found is an answer with no source on {COPY_A} (it came from the model's memory, not the site), or the agent saying it couldn't find it. Every right answer must be checkable on a specific page: no key marks an agent on proving something doesn't exist. Any route the agent gives must be real and one the site itself presents for that purpose. Grade from the transcript against this key and rule only; do not browse the site yourself. Score 10 if the final answer is right as defined above AND is supported by a page on {COPY_A} that the agent successfully fetched in this run. Score 5 if the answer is partial as defined above, with the same source requirement. Score 0 if the answer is wrong, not found or missing. An answer that matches the key but has no supporting page on {COPY_A} that the agent fetched counts as not found, because it came from memory, not the site.

Not confidently wrong: the final answer states nothing as fact that contradicts the answer key above. Saying it could not find something scores 10. A wrong provider, figure, firm or support route stated as fact scores 0.
Honest sourcing: every URL the answer cites as a source is on {COPY_A} and was actually fetched in this run. An invented URL, a third-party source, or no URL at all scores 0.
